Summary
Monterrey driver strike addressed with trip blocks and recruitment plans alongside schedule confirmations
Monterrey Driver Strike: Management decided to stop assigning trips to striking drivers. Striking drivers were blocked from viewing trip offerings related to Tesla and Ford to prevent protests.
Recruitment and Kavak Schedule: Driver shortages prompted plans to recruit new drivers by distributing cards to Uber drivers. Kavak schedule is set for November 15th, superseding the earlier inquiry.
Employee Onboarding Adjustments: Higher date is registered as September 2nd, and teams are working on retroactive adjustments. Daily follow-ups are occurring with the unresponsive group to resolve delays.

Monterrey driver strike and recruitment
- Julia Diaz reported that approximately 15 drivers in Monterrey are organizing a strike.
- Management blocked striking drivers from viewing Tesla and Ford trips to prevent facility disruptions.
- The team is actively recruiting new drivers in Monterrey using app cards and referrals.
- A severe driver shortage in Monterrey creates ongoing difficulties for moving vehicles.

Kavak timeline and legal review
- Jaqueline Sanches scheduled the Kavak implementation timeline for November 15.
- A 4 PM meeting with Mexico legal counsel will provide visibility on ongoing office issues.

Onboarding and retroactive date adjustments
- Employee onboarding and registration are completed with a temporary start date of September 2.
- Jaqueline Sanches is following up daily to secure official start date adjustments and retroactive processing.

Details
Monterrey Driver Strike and Trip Restrictions: Julia Diaz brings up an upcoming business trip to Monterrey due to an issue where approximately 15 drivers are organizing a strike and refusing to take trips. Julia Diaz explains that management decided to stop assigning trips to these individuals. To prevent potential protests at customer facilities, Julia Diaz states they blocked the striking drivers from viewing trip offerings related to Tesla and Ford. Additionally, Jaqueline Sanches mentions receiving a message on LinkedIn from one of the involved drivers named Jose Reyes.

Monterrey Driver Recruitment and Kavak Schedule: Julia Diaz notes that the driver shortage creates difficulties in moving cars in Monterrey, and outlines plans to recruit new drivers by distributing cards to Uber drivers and utilizing word-of-mouth networks. Regarding Kavak, Jaqueline Sanches states that the schedule is set for November 15th, superseding an earlier inquiry about November 2nd. Jaqueline Sanches explains that once Julia Diaz communicates this personally, Jaqueline Sanches will share the necessary documents via DocuSign. Furthermore, Jaqueline Sanches mentions a 4 PM meeting scheduled with legal counsel from the Mexico office to discuss related matters.

Employee Onboarding Adjustments and Follow-Up Delays: Jaqueline Sanches states that the higher date is registered as September 2nd, and they are actively working on retroactive adjustments. Julia Diaz notes that onboarding is completed, but they are still waiting on official adjustments to start dates after submitting all requested information. Jaqueline Sanches states that they have been following up daily with the unresponsive group to resolve the delays.
